assessment: The ten builds the width plan a piece at a time: two more cards that turn a token entering into damage, three more sources of tokens, one draw engine paid by tokens, and the ramp that casts them. The bench is 34 entries and it prunes hard before ranking starts — two are the sleeved copies of cards already in the 99, one sits outside Edgar's colour identity, the obsolescence index puts two more behind cards already on the battlefield, and roughly a dozen are Blood-token or sacrifice filler that the deck's direction rules out. Four bench cards survive that and make the list; six pool cards beat what was left of the tail, and each names the bench card it displaced. Per strategy:critical-mass, "the deck's defense is speed, redundancy, and resilience, not answers" — which is why six of the ten cuts come out of the interaction suite or the aristocrats package rather than out of the engine.

combo_lines_opened.produces: damage to each opponent per Vampire cast, scaled by both token doublers

ten.closes: Purphoros, God of the Forge (1 card)
ten.why: Purphoros is the only card in the 99 that turns a token entering into damage, and stack 008 measured it at 10 to each opponent per two-mana Vampire cast; Impact Tremors is that trigger for {1}{R}, so the kill becomes something you draw rather than something you tutor for.
ten.unlocks: A second non-combat clock on the cheapest rung of the curve. It also makes the plan legible against the corpus's warning that "~120 combined life behind three defenses makes incremental combat damage a losing plan" (strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry).

ten.why: Every token source in the deck needs the pilot to be casting or attacking, so the board stops growing the moment the hand empties; the Conqueror makes a 1/1 lifelink Vampire on the opponents' turns instead, every time one of them lands an untapped creature or artifact and declines to tap it.
ten.when: Sleeve it first. It is a two-mana Vampire, so casting it is already two bodies, and the tokens it makes are Vampires — Legion Lieutenant, Stromkirk Captain and Sanctum Seeker all count them.

ten.why: Three counted draw pieces against a template of ten, and none of them rebuilds a board that is gone; the Talent draws whenever tokens enter — once a turn, which is every turn Edgar is anywhere — and it is an enchantment, so a wrath does not take it with the board.
ten.unlocks: Level 2 copies a token and level 3 makes every creature token +2/+2, so the same slot is a fifth token source and a mass pump. It beats Markov Purifier off the bench: both are draw engines, but the Purifier charges {2} at each end step and the obsolescence index lists Preacher of the Schism — already sleeved — among its replacements.

combo_lines_opened.produces: damage to each opponent per Vampire cast, plus a static anthem on the tokens

ten.closes: Purphoros, God of the Forge (1 card)
ten.why: The only card in the archetype that is an anthem and a width payoff at once: every 1/1 token enters as a 2/2 before Edgar's attack counters, and every entry pings each opponent for 1.
ten.unlocks: Redundancy on the deck's highest-leverage effect, which per strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors is the cheap purchase — "5 copies is 31% of openers, 7 is 41%". Price the mana honestly: {1}{R}{W} wants two off-black colours in a deck with 16 red and 18 white sources against 25 black.

ten.card: Legion's Landing // Adanto, the First Fort
ten.why: One white mana makes a 1/1 lifelink Vampire immediately, and a deck with 18 two-drops and an eminence trigger attacks with three creatures early enough that the flip is routine; Adanto then makes another Vampire every turn for {2}{W}.
ten.unlocks: A token source a wrath cannot answer — the land side is not a creature — and a mana source that costs a spell slot rather than a land slot, in a deck already sitting at 37 lands against a 34-36 band. It beats Unholy Officiant off the bench: same one-mana white rung, but the Officiant is a vanilla body and this is a repeatable token factory.

combo_lines_opened.produces: eight Vampire tokens from a single eminence trigger

ten.why: Stack 002 measured one eminence trigger as four bodies through Anointed Procession and Mondrak; a third doubler is the card that makes it eight, and her 0 puts a +1/+1 counter on each creature and grants them flying until your next turn.
ten.unlocks: The alpha strike the deck otherwise has to earn, on a permanent that also answers a blocker with -3. Five mana is the top of what this curve should take, so this is the one pick that raises the top end. It beats Vampire Nocturnus off the bench: same mass-evasion job, no BBB and no coin flip on the top card.

ten.why: A go-wide deck folding to one wrath is the trap, and Elenda is the only card on the bench that answers it: she grows on every creature that dies anywhere, and when she dies she leaves X 1/1 lifelink Vampires — 2X through Anointed Procession, 4X through both doublers.
ten.when: Sleeve it when the pod runs two or more sweepers. Read the trigger before trusting it: the payoff fires on her death, but what it pays out is width, not drain, and the tokens are Vampires the lords already buff.

ten.why: Ramp counts seven against a template of ten and two of the seven are on their way out of the deck; the Banner taps for any colour, which is the only kind of acceleration that also helps black at 25 sources against a 36-source yardstick, and it anthems every Vampire while it sits there.
ten.unlocks: Typal mana in the shape this deck wants — the synergy graph pairs it with Herald's Horn as ramp next to cost reduction, and neither asks the pilot to spend a land slot. It beats Akroma's Memorial off the bench: both are colourless team-wide artifacts, but seven mana has no rung on a curve whose mode is two.

ten.why: Creature, artifact, enchantment and land are covered eleven, three, three and two deep; graveyard is covered zero, and this is the only card on the bench that touches it — on a two-mana first-striking Vampire, so the floor is a body plus an eminence token.
ten.when: Sleeve it against a reanimator or self-mill seat. Exile a land or an instant, never a creature card: the ongoing trigger is symmetric and this deck casts creatures every turn. It moves interaction-breadth from four to five and graveyard from zero to one — one card, once.

ten.why: Edgar's attack trigger puts a +1/+1 counter on each Vampire in the declare-attackers step, and the Falconer turns every one of those counters into flying before blockers — so the alpha strike lands the turn Edgar swings rather than the turn the board finally outnumbers three defences.
ten.when: Sleeve it when the pod blocks well on the ground. Cover of Darkness already grants fear, which any black creature blanks; flying is the version that does not care, and the slot comes out of an interaction suite the audit reads at twelve against an aggro target of five to six.

bench_verdicts.card: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
bench_verdicts.why: Already sleeved in the 99 — the bench entry is that same card, not a second copy.
Same: it is in the maindeck, so the bench line is bookkeeping rather than a candidate.

bench_verdicts.card: Runo Stromkirk // Krothuss, Lord of the Deep
bench_verdicts.why: Blue, and Edgar's colour identity is Mardu — unplayable here at any power level.

The obsolescence index lists Bloodline Keeper // Lord of Lineage as strictly better and that card is already on the battlefield; reading both, the Keeper makes a 2/2 flying Vampire every turn while the Nocturnus needs BBB and a black top card.
The index names Preacher of the Schism among its replacements, and the Preacher is already sleeved; the Purifier's draw also costs {2} at each end step.
Duplicated function: Stromkirk Captain already gives every Vampire first strike, so the Masquerade is paying three mana for a +1/+1 counter on connection.
The ninth lord. Convoke makes it nearly free off a wide board, but the lord package already assembles 77.2% of games at a mean turn of 2.74 — that is the one component that needs nothing.
Seven mana in a deck whose modal mana value is two and whose top card is six. The effect is real; the rung does not exist.

Not in the scan, so it is an order rather than a box — and worth naming, because its mode exiles a whole graveyard where Cemetery Gatekeeper takes one card. Three mana for a modal body is the wrong rung; if the pilot wants the bigger graveyard answer, buy this one.
Also absent from the scan. The draw half needs you to have gained 2 life that turn, which is a condition, not an engine.
Ramp that eats a creature. The direction is width; converting a body into mana runs the other way.
A sacrifice outlet whose payoff is counters. With the aristocrats package leaving there is nothing on the other side of the outlet.
Draws by sacrificing another creature — the exact trade the deck is being built to stop making.
Counters that arrive when creatures die. It is a death payoff wearing an equipment's clothes.
Its token half is a graveyard activation, and Bats are not Vampires — no lord buffs them and Sanctum Seeker does not count them.
Transforms when you attack with exactly two creatures. This deck attacks with six.
A narrow tutor in a deck the audit already reads adequate at three, and the pump it grants is single-target.

bench_verdicts.card: Sorin of House Markov // Sorin, Ravenous Neonate
bench_verdicts.why: A Human Noble, so casting it makes no eminence token, and both halves pay in lifegain-drain rather than bodies.

bench_verdicts.card: Aclazotz, Deepest Betrayal // Temple of the Dead
bench_verdicts.why: Five mana whose Bats depend on opponents discarding lands, and whose death clause is a return from the graveyard.
A blocker. Deathtouch and lifelink defend; nothing here makes the board wider or the width hurt more.
The same card at two mana, and the same objection: this deck is the archenemy from turn two and wins by attacking.
A 2/1 flier that cannot block. Cheap Vampires are two bodies each, but this one adds nothing the 18 two-drops already sleeved do not.
One mana for a Vampire and a token is a real rate; the card does nothing else, and the same rung buys a repeatable token factory instead.
Intimidate on one target per trigger. The deck's evasion problem is a team problem.
cards.csv carries no oracle text for it, so this is read off the printed faces: a deathtouch granter whose second half is an X drain. Neither half makes or uses width.
Blood tokens are artifacts. They do not attack, no lord buffs them, and Edgar's counters skip them.
Same currency, and it has to connect first to earn it.
Its Blood token arrives when it dies — a death trigger that pays in artifacts.
Five mana for an attack trigger that spends a Blood token the deck has no reason to be making.
Blood and discard payoffs in a deck with no discard theme; the counters are on one creature.

gaps: Every combo line in the ten is unverified. Impact Tremors and Warleader's Call through Anointed Procession and Mondrak both need a /resolve-stack run: stack 008 settled the entry count for a 2-damage trigger on Purphoros, not for a 1-damage pinger, and whether the Call's +1/+1 applies to tokens created by the same eminence trigger is unsettled.

The pool's combo-opener channel is unusable for this deck. All 25 openers hang off Exquisite Blood or Bloodthirsty Conqueror lifegain loops; the first of those is leaving the deck and the direction points away from the rest, so no pick here was ranked on a combo count.

The synergy channel found almost nothing usable: 25 candidates and every one of them an 'Aura + Protection' edge hanging off Swiftfoot Boots and Teferi's Protection — a format-wide shortlist locating this deck's protection spells rather than its engines. One claim survived, Patchwork Banner next to Herald's Horn.

Three bench cards are not in the pilot's scan and their availability is unconfirmed: Callous Bloodmage, Runo Stromkirk // Krothuss and Scheming Silvertongue // Sign in Blood. None of the three is in the ten. Callous Bloodmage is the one worth a decision — its mode exiles an entire graveyard where the Gatekeeper exiles one card.

colour-sources is the measured weakness the ten only glances at. Black reads 25 against a 36-source yardstick and Patchwork Banner is the only pick that touches it. That is a manabase job, no bench card is a land, and the audit's own note says the 25 is a floor — four fetchlands, Reflecting Pool and Urborg all really produce black and all score zero.

card-advantage carries a probe note, so it is a question as much as a hole: Minas Tirith and Castle Locthwain are repeatable activated draws, Preacher of the Schism draws on attack and Midgar's adventure half draws two, none of them inside the counted 3. That is why one draw engine is on this list and not three.

No verified line exists for the token plan's kill. Stacks 002, 003, 007 and 008 measure tokens per cast, drain per attack, drain per end step and damage per cast; none of them is a scenario in which the deck wins, and the checker-passed kills the deck does have rest on Exquisite Blood.
The bench carries no EDHREC rank for a single one of its 34 entries, so nothing here is ranked on popularity — bench picks rest on the deck's own measured deficits and on oracle text.
